user.title: Private Integrations
user.description:
Paste a GitHub Personal Access Token. Two ways to create one:

- **[Classic PAT (pre-filled with 'repo' scope)]({classic_url})** — works for any private repo your account can access.
- **[Fine-grained PAT]({fine_url})** — more secure: scope it to only the specific repos you want to install, with **Repository permissions → Contents: Read-only**.

The token is stored in the config entry, which Home Assistant keeps in `.storage/core.config_entries` as plain JSON: it is redacted from the API but not encrypted, so treat your backups as secrets.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate Private Integrations
reauth_confirm.description: The current GitHub token is no longer valid. Paste a new one. You can [create a classic PAT]({classic_url}) or a [fine-grained PAT]({fine_url}).

init.title: Private Integrations
init.description: What would you like to do?

menu_options.manage_repository: Manage / install / update a tracked repository

add_repository.title: Add a private repository
add_repository.description:
Paste the GitHub repository URL or 'owner/repo', then choose how to track it.

_After a successful install you will need to restart Home Assistant for the new integration to load. A persistent notification will remind you._

data.ref: Tag / branch / commit (leave blank for the default branch)
data.integration_name: Integration folder name (only if the repo has multiple)

manage_repository.title: Pick a tracked repository
manage_repository.description: Choose which repository to act on.

repository_action.title: {repo}
repository_action.description:
Pick an action. **Install / update** writes to `custom_components/` and requires a Home Assistant restart to take effect.

{notice}

installed_confirmation.title: Installed
installed_confirmation.description:
**{repo}** is installed as `custom_components/{integration}/` (version: `{version}`).

## Restart required

Home Assistant must be **restarted** for the new integration to load. The files are on disk but not yet active.

Go to **Developer Tools → YAML → Restart**, or use the system menu.

Click **Submit** to close this dialog.

update_token.title: Update GitHub token
update_token.description: Replace the stored token with a new Personal Access Token.

edit_repository.title: {repo}
edit_repository.description:
Change how this repository is followed: latest `release`, a `tag`, a `branch` or a pinned `commit`, and which folder it installs into.

Nothing is downloaded here — run **Install / update** afterwards to apply the new ref.

data.ref: Tag / branch / commit (required unless tracking a release)
data.integration_name: Integration folder name (leave blank to use the only one in the repo)

confirm_remove.title: {repo}
confirm_remove.description:
Stop tracking this repository.

Leave **Delete installed files** checked to remove `custom_components/{integration}/` as well. Uncheck it to keep the files on disk (Home Assistant keeps running the current version).

tracked_confirmation.title: Repository added
tracked_confirmation.description:
**{repo}** is now tracked.

Nothing was downloaded. Run **Install / update** from the previous screen when you want its files in `custom_components/`.

removed_confirmation.title: Repository removed
removed_confirmation.description:
**{repo}** is no longer tracked and its files {files}.

If the integration was loaded, it keeps running until you restart Home Assistant; a restart makes it disappear from the loaded integrations.

install_failed.title: Added, but not installed

abort.no_repositories: No repositories are tracked yet. Add one first.

common.tracking_saved: **{repo}** saved. Nothing has been downloaded yet: run **Install / update** to apply it.
common.install_notification:
**{repo}** has been installed as `custom_components/{integration}/` (version: `{version}`).

**Restart Home Assistant** to load the new integration. Until you restart, the files are on disk but not yet active.

add_repository.name: Add repository
add_repository.description: Track a GitHub repository so it can be installed and kept up to date.

ref_type.name: Ref type
ref_type.description: Which kind of GitHub ref to follow.

ref.name: Ref
ref.description: Specific tag name, branch name, or commit SHA. Leave blank to follow the repository's default branch (ref_type=branch) or the latest release (ref_type=release).

integration_name.name: Integration name
integration_name.description: Folder name under custom_components/ to install. Required only if the repo contains more than one integration.

remove_repository.name: Remove repository
remove_repository.description: Stop tracking a repository and delete its installed files. Only files installed by this integration are deleted.

delete_files.name: Delete installed files
delete_files.description: Also remove the integration folder under custom_components/. Disable it to stop tracking a repository and keep its files.

install.name: Install
install.description: Download a tracked repository and write it into custom_components/. A Home Assistant restart is required to load the new integration.

force.name: Force reinstall
force.description: Install even when the tracked ref already resolves to the version on disk.

update.name: Update
update.description: Re-install a tracked repository at its current ref (typically picking up a new release or branch HEAD). Restart Home Assistant after running.
